data.name: Antaryami
data.long_meaning: Antaryami is a Sanskrit name derived from the term 'antar' meaning 'inner' and 'yami' meaning 'ruler' or 'master'. This name is given to a child who is believed to be an inner ruler or an inner master, one who has the power to control their own thoughts, emotions, and actions.

The name also inspires a sense of self-reliance and the belief that one has the power and potential to govern themselves.

The name also reminds one of their innate connection to the divine and encourages them to tap into their inner wisdom and intuition.

historical_references.reference: Antaryami is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata, in the context of the Yoga of Knowledge or Jnana Yoga. According to the text, the sage Vyasa, the author of the Mahabharata, described the Self as the Antaryami, the inner controller, the innermost being, or the witness consciousness within every being.

The term Antaryami is also used in the Bhagavad Gita, where it is described as the supreme controller within every individual soul. This concept is often referred to as the 'inner controller' or 'inner lord'.
